Best Clean Protein Bars - Ranking 485 Bars by Ingredient Quality

We rank the cleanest protein bars by category, brand, and macros. Not just us telling you the flavors we like.

What "clean" actually means on this page

Clean is three separate screens stacked together, not one soft label. A bar has to clear all three to make this list: an A or B ingredient quality grade, no artificial sweeteners, and no processed oils.

58.9% of the 1181 bars in our database fail at least one of these. Here's how often each screen catches a bar, and where it usually shows up.

Ingredient Quality Grade C or Below
541 bars45.8%
The most common reason a bar fails the clean screen. A C, D, or F grade usually means synthetic additives, excess added sugar, or ultra-processed protein blends outweighing the ingredient list's strengths.
Affects: at least one flavor from 95 of 165 brands we track
Artificial Sweeteners
241 bars20.4%
Usually shows up as a flavor-rounding sweetener in low-sugar or high-fiber bars, often alongside allulose or fiber syrups to hit a specific sugar number on the label.
Found in: 1st Phorm, Addra Labs, Anabar, Atkins

Processed Oils
473 bars40.1%
Usually a refined oil like canola, soybean, palm, or a hydrogenated fat used for shelf stability or texture, not nutrition.

What we found screening 1181 bars for clean criteria

58.9%
of bars fail at least one clean criterion
696 of 1181 bars fail the ingredient grade, the artificial sweetener screen, the processed oil screen, or some combination of the three. 416 of those fail more than one screen at once.
Processed oils disqualify almost as many bars as low grades.
473 bars (40.1%) contain a processed oil, not far behind the 541 bars (45.8%) that score a C grade or below. Between the two, ingredient-list quality problems outnumber sweetener problems by a wide margin.
Most disqualified bars fail more than one screen.
416 of the 696 disqualified bars fail two or all three criteria at once. Only 149 fail on grade alone, 98 on processed oils alone, and just 33 on artificial sweeteners alone.
Barebells and Quest fail completely.
Every tracked flavor from both brands contains an artificial sweetener and a processed oil, and most also score C or below. Neither brand has a single flavor that clears the clean screen.
Whole-food brands dominate the qualifying pool.
Larabar, Perfect Bar, Healthy Eating on the Go, Kize, RXBAR, and Bearded Bros all qualify at or near 100%, mostly built around dates, nuts, and whole-food protein sources instead of processed blends.
A mixed lineup is common.
NuGo qualifies at 20% (6 of 30 flavors), KIND at just 6.5% (2 of 31). Even brands with a reputation for clean eating rarely clear the bar across their entire lineup.
Disqualified bars average more protein than qualifying ones.
Bars that fail the clean screen average 14.6g protein versus 11.4g for bars that pass, a reminder that higher protein numbers often come from processed protein blends and synthetic sweeteners doing the work.
97 of 165 brands still clear at least one flavor.
Even with 58.9% of the database disqualified, more than half of the brands we track have at least one bar that passes all three clean criteria.

Frequently asked questions

For this guide, clean means three things at once: an A or B ingredient quality grade, no artificial sweeteners (sucralose, acesulfame potassium, aspartame, saccharin), and no processed oils (canola, soybean, palm, or hydrogenated oils). 485 of 1181 bars in our database meet all three criteria.
Cleaner ingredients generally means fewer synthetic additives, more whole-food protein sources, and less dependence on ultra-processed fats and sweeteners. That said, macros still matter. A clean bar can still be high in calories or sugar even if the ingredient list is excellent.
416 of the 696 disqualified bars fail more than one criterion at once, usually a processed oil and a below-B grade together. Manufacturers reach for cheap refined oils and synthetic sweeteners to hit specific price, shelf-life, or macro targets, and those same shortcuts tend to drag the ingredient score down too.
No. Every tracked flavor from both brands contains an artificial sweetener and a processed oil, and most also score C or below on ingredient quality. Neither brand has a single flavor that clears this guide's screen.
485 bars across 97 brands clear our clean screen, led by whole-food brands like Larabar, Perfect Bar, and Healthy Eating on the Go that qualify at or near 100%. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
It depends on your standard. Erythritol is a naturally occurring sugar alcohol, but commercially it's derived through fermentation of glucose, often from corn. We score it as a neutral-to-minor concern rather than an automatic disqualifier, so bars with erythritol can still earn A or B grades and appear on this list if the rest of the ingredient list is strong.
Egg whites, whey protein concentrate, and whole-food sources like nuts and seeds score highest. Whey isolate and pea protein score slightly lower but are still solid. Collagen protein scores as a concern because it lacks the essential amino acids needed for muscle protein synthesis.
Yes, and it's common. NuGo qualifies at 20% (6 of 30 flavors), KIND at just 6.5% (2 of 31). Check the Mixed Lineups table below before assuming a brand's whole lineup is clean just because one flavor is.
We update the database when new bars are added or when brands change their formulas. The scoring methodology stays consistent so grades are comparable across updates. The current data reflects August 2026.
